List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Environment and
Forests; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Ocean Development; Railways;

Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—20
Drought in  Southern States
*61. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO:
SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost all
the Southern States  particularly Karnataka
and Kerala are in the grip of worst drought
this year;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) whether any Central team has visited
the States to assess the drought situation
there;
(d) if so, the findings thereof; and
(e) what relief measures have been
extended to the affected States so far,
State-wise?
Air-pollution in metros
†*62.  SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of EN VIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
air-pollution is increasing day by day in
the four metropolitan cities i.e. Delhi,
Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the date of the last study on pollution
in each of these metros;
(d) whether any fresh study is proposed
to be conducted; and
(e) whether any time-bound programme
has been prepared to reduce pollution and
if so, the details thereof?
ADB funds for Railway projects
*63. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fa ct that the Asian
Development Bank has agreed to Fund
some Railway projects;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

20
(b) if so, the details of the projects;
(c) the quantum of the assistance being
extended by the ADB; and
(d) the list of the externally aided
projects and details of the loan taken from
various agencies other than ADB?
Education for All-Global
monitoring report
*64. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ:
 DR. MANMOHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether he is aware of the fact that
UNESCO's latest Education For All (EFA)
global monitoring report says that
Bangladesh has achieved gender parity equal
enrolment of boys and girls at school at the
Primary level and India scraps the
bottom of the list just a little above
Pakistan; and
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Objectives of National Education
Policy
*65. DR. MANMOHAN SINGH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the trend of public expenditure on
education expressed as a percentage of GDP
and total public expenditure since 1990;
and
(b) whether this trend is consistent with
the resource requirements for
meeting the National Education Policy
objectives?
Mid-Day Meal Scheme
*66. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Mid-Day Meal Scheme has
been expanded  further throughout the
country;
(b) if so, whether many opposition
parties have also urged Centre to expand
Mid-Day Meal Scheme;
(c) whether mid-day meal supplied in
Delhi and other places have been found
affecting children instead of helping them;
(d) if so, whether Centre has been
informed that in number of States, after
mid-day meal were supplied, number of
children had been forced to go to hospitals;
(e) the total number of students who
were affected due to this; and
(f) the steps Government propose to
take to prevent such incidents in future?
Degrees to students of G.S.B.A.,
Greater Noida
*67. SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to refer to  answers to Unstarred
Question 2824 and 4737 given in Rajya
Sabha on the 17th August, 2001 and 10th
May, 2002 respectively and state:
(a) the reasons for delay in awarding
'Degrees' to successful students who have
already completed the Masters in
Computer Application course in July, 2003
in the 'Approved' institute at Graduate
School of Business Administration, Greater
Noida;

21
(b) the details of steps initiated/likely
to be taken to honour the commitments
already made by Visva Bharti,
Shantiniketan to safeguard the interests of
successful students of the batch passing
out in July, 2003 already enrolled at
Graduate School of  Business
Administration, Greater Noida; and
(c) by when, the final Marks Statement
and Degree Certificates are likely to be
issued to them?
Expansion and growth of FPIs
†*68. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision to implement a time-bound scheme
for expansion and growth of food
processing industry in the country so that
fruits and vegetables worth Rs. 50,000 crore
could be saved from being perished without
being used;
(b) if so, the scheme of the Government
in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that instead of
given tax-relief to this industry for its
expansion, the taxes have been increased
during preceding years; and
(d) if so, the facts in this regard?
Auxillary Warning System in
Railways
*69. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Railway is planning to
adopt a new Auxillary Warning System to
strengthen the safety and security of
passengers and ra il installations;
(b) what is the difference between AWS
and the train protection and warning
system recommended by Khanna
Committee; and
(c) how the outside interference with
rail installations such as track and signalling
equipment is likely to be curtailed with the
help of the above warning system?
Dress code for girl students in
Universities
†*70.  SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some
Universities have prescribed dress code for
the girl students;
(b) if so, the justification thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that girl
students are opposing the said move;
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(e) the action proposed to be taken by
Government against the Vice-Chancellors
of such Universities?
East Coast Railway Head quarters
*71. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that East Coast
Railway has not yet become functional and
many trains including Rajdhani Express
which are operating from Bhubaneswar are
being controlled by GM, Railway, Garden
Reach, Kolkata;
(b) total number of staff and officers
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

22
required for East Coast Railway
Headquarters and the total staff in position;
and
(c) total budget allocation for East
Coast Railway Zone and year-wise
allocation till today?
Promotion of organic farming
*72. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN:
SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state the steps taken or
proposed to be taken for promoting ogranic
farming by safeguarding chemical poisoning
of food and water in the country and making
agricultural activity more eco-friendly?
Suggestions for reviewing the
Dowry Prohibition Act
*73. SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH
LIBRA:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
suggestions from various women
organisations for reviewing the Dowry
Prohibition Act to make its provisions
more stringent and effective;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
raise the status of women?
Bharat Shiksha Kosh
*74.SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the total amount collected in Bharat
Shiksha Kosh since its inception;
(b) whether it is a fact that many of the
donors are opposing to pass donations
through BSK;
(c) if so, how Government are planning
to deal with the situation; and
(d) the amount disbursed through BSK
to various institutions of the country;
institution-wise?
Fishing harbour projects of
Karnataka
*75. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the projects for construction
of Karwar Fishing Harbour and Malpe
Fishing Harbour of Karnataka Government,
at an estimated cost of Rs. 229 lakhs and
Rs. 481.65 lakhs respectively, are pending
with Central Government for approval; and
(b) if so, the details of the projects and
the time by which these are likely to be
cleared?
Use of Naptha fuel and gas as fuel
†*76. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Naptha, fuel
oil and gas is used as fuel for production of
urea fertilizer in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
the cost of production has been found to
be varying based on the fuel used in
production;
(c) if so, the cost of production of urea
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

23
produced during the production year
2002-2003  calculated on the basis of use
of Naptha, fuel oil and gas separately; and
(d) the perce ntage of each of the said
fuels being used at present in the country
by fertilizer industry?
Review of Pharmaceutical
Policy 2002
*77. SHRI VAYALAR RAVI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to review the Pharmaceutical Policy 2002;
(b) if so, whether Standing Committee
on Petroleum and Chemicals has suggested
the Ministry to have a re-look at new policy
and endeavour to make it widely acceptable
and free of legal lacunae;
(c) whether panel has pointed out that
the policy was not people friendly and even
Supreme Court has commented adversely
on it;
(d) if so, whether the Court had also
refused to permit operationalisation of drug
price control order under the new policy;
and
(e) by when final decision in this regard
is likely to be taken?
World Bank study on pollution
level in Ganga river
*78. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether as per a study sponsored
by the World Bank, the pollution level in
the Ganga river continue to be alarmingly
high Contributing to nearly 12 per cent of
the total disease burden in the State of Uttar
Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto;
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
reduce the pollution of the river to the
minimum index level set by the National
Science Foundation; and
(d) the other major findings of the World
Bank evaluation study and Government's
reaction thereto?
Consideration of disinvestment of
NFL
*79. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the considera-
tion of disinvestment of National Fertilizer
Ltd. has been put-off for two years;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) was Government able to secure bids
for reserve price; and
(d) if not, steps being taken to improve
the performance of NFL to attract better
offers?
Public sector investment in
agriculture production
*80. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the agriculture
production in the country is showing a
downward trend since 1991 particularly
after 1996-97;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the Public

24
Sector investment in agriculture declined
considerably during this period;
(d) if so, the year-wise details of Public
Sector investment in agriculture during the
years 1991—2002;
(e) the comparative figures of
investment during the years 1980—90;
(f) whether the low investment by
Public Sector negatively affect the growth
and competitiveness of this sector; and
(g) the response of Government
thereto?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 29th November, 2003 Secretary-General.

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

(Ministries :  Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Environment and
Forests; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development;
Ocean Development; Railways; Science and Technology; Steel;
Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—143
Price support for saffron crop
342. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that for the first time in four years,
Kishtwar’s saffron farmers are expecting a
good saffron crop;
(b) if so, whether Government have
noticed the fact that official neglect has hit
the farmers' interests hard and they rarely
get the attention and the prices they deserve;
and
(c) if so, the efforts, Government
propose  to make the Government-run
price support mechanism available for the
benefit of such farmers?
Assistance to Andhra Pradesh
from NCCF
343. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh
Assembly has passed a unanimous
resolution requesting the Central
Government to immediately release
Rs. 996.12 crores from National
Calamity Contingency Fund and 15 lakh
tonnes of rice under the Swarna Jayanti
Grameen Rozgar Yojana to meet the need
of drought affected areas of the
State; and
(b) if so, the response of the Central
Government in this regard?
Promotion of organic farming
344. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
Government have formulated a national
project on organic farming with an outlay
of Rs. 99.58 crore to improve the soil
health;
(b) whether the project envisages the
setting up of National Institute of Organic
Farming (NIOF) for the production,
promotion, market development and
regulation of organic farming in the country;
and
(c) if so, the details of the proposed
scheme?

76
Agriculture research and education
centres
345. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question 1343, given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 1st August, 2003
and state:
(a) the details of basic infrastructure
provided by the agriculture research and
education centres; and
(b) the steps taken by Government to
upgrade these research centres?
Insurance cover for yield and
price fluctuations
346. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce a new insurance cover for yield
and price fluctuations for farmers under a
single policy;
(b) if so, the details of the scheme; and
(c) by when it is likely to be put in
operation?
Assistance to SC/ST farmers of
M.P.
347. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to release the fund from the contingency
fund to help the SCs/STs and Backward
agriculturists in Madhya Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Assistance to pest affected
district Malkangiri, Orissa
348. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that over 5000
families of farmers in the tribal dominated
Malkangiri district of Orissa were in
distress, on account of pest attacks on their
crops which had, in turn, affected their
livelihood; and
(b) whether the Centre has offered
assistance to the cash-strapped State to
compensate the affected farmers; if so, the
details thereof?
All day milk stalls of DMS
349. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there are many DMS outlets
running in Delhi by the name of 'All Day
Milk Stalls’;
(b) if so, whether these outlets have been
opened as franchisee of DMS;
(c) if so, the number of outlets that are
running in Delhi; and
(d) the amount of revenue earned by
DMS as franchise deposits?
Survey of wheat varieties
350. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a survey of
wheat varieties suitable for overseas market
as well as for better yield is being conducted;
(b) if so, the result of such exercise;

77
(c) by when Government propose to
introduce such varieties for commercial
production; and
(d) the details thereof?
Boosting sale of DMS milk
351. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the percentage of milk in polypacks
returned to Delhi Milk Scheme during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) the additional expenditure incurred
in reprocessing of these polypacks;
(c) whether the sale of milk had
decreased as a result of increase in prices
and if so, the action taken to reduce it and
boosting the sale; and
(d) the distribution losses reported
during the last three years?
Shortage of milk in Delhi
352. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there was an
acute shortage of milk in Delhi during last
August;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor, especially
in view of  higher yield of milk by the milch
animals in the area around Delhi during
monsoon which was above average this
year; and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
to ensure that the capital does not face
shortage of milk in future, particularly during
the festival season?
Agriculture Technology Information
Centres in U.P.
353. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of Agriculture Technology
Information Centres set up in Uttar
Pradesh, district-wise;
(b) the details of expenditure incurred
by Government for the above purpose
during the last three years; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
provide training to farmers about the new
technology?
Incentives to producers of export
quality Basmati rice
†354. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the names of States which are
producing export quality Basmati rice
alongwith the details of the total production
of such Basmati rice in the country every
year;
(b) whether any scheme has been
formulated by Government to provide
incentives to the States producing such
Basmati rice; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Agricultural contribution to GDP
355. SHRI DINA NATH MISHRA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) how much agriculture sector is likely
to contribute to country's total GDP in the
year 2003-04;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

78
(b) what would be its share in economic
growth in percentage terms during the same
period; and
(c) what future steps Government are
initiating to strengthen infrastructure, so
as to considerably enhance agricultural
production during the Tenth Five Year Plan?
Assistance to agricultural projects of
States
356. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state the
details of financial assistance provided by
the Central Government to the States, West
Bengal in particular, during the last two
years for the development and upgradation
of agricultural projects?
Agricultural production vis-a-vis
rainfall
357. SHRI S. AGNIRAJ: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the total level of rainfall in the
country during the monsoon;
(b) the likely fall in the levels during
this season; and
(c) its impact on agricultural production
during this year?
KVKs in Tripura
358. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the status of setting up of Krishi
Vigyan Kendras in each district of Tripura;
(b) the places of the State where these
Kendras are going to be established; and
(c) the reasons for the delay in
establishing these Kendras and the period
by which they would be made functional?
Agricultural University in Tripura
359. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government are
going to set up an Agricultural University
in Tripura; and
(b) if so, by when?
Agricultural performance
360. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite all
natural advantages, India's productivity of
foodgrains per hectare is no more than three-
fourth of the world average and less than
half of that in agriculturally advanced
countries;
(b) whether only five States namely
Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar
Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, produce
more grains than their requirement and more
than two-third of the population lives in
States that are still food-deficit;
(c) if so, whether Government have
made efforts to find the reasons for its poor
agricultural performance; and
(d) the action Government propose to
take in this regard?
Starvation deaths
361. DR. AKHILESH DAS: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any reports of starvation deaths from Bihar,

79
Orissa, Andhra Pradesh and other States
during the current year;
(b) if so, the details of such reports from
different States; and
(c) whether it is a fact that State
Governments usually discount starvation
deaths and find alibis saying deaths were
not due to hunger but due to lack of medical
facilities and different ailments like diarrhoea,
caused by under nourishment?
Drip irrigation technology
362. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Union Government have
taken any step or propose to take any step
for providing new, effective and cheapest
technology for the drip irrigation everywhere
in the country to the farmers;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that Netafim, an
Israeli firm with pioneering expertise in drip
irrigation, has tied up with some Indian
banks to facilitate loans for drip irrigation
projects in the country; and
(d) if so, Government’s response thereto?
Donation to Consultative Group on
International Agricultural
Research
†363. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN
SINGH 'LALAN':
SHRI  RAM  JETHMALANI:
SHRI  LAJPAT  RAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a proposal of providing an
additional donation of ten million dollars
to Consultative Group on International
Agricultural Research is under consideration
during the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) if so, the amount of regular donation
being given annually to the institution;
(c) whether the operation of the said
institute is being carried out from abroad;
(d) if so, the place of operation and the
details of agricultural activities of the said
institute;
(e) whether the country has got any
advantage from the research conducted by
this institution; and
(f) if so, the benefits accrued to Indian
farmers from this institution for the
development in the agriculture sector?
Effect of subsidy given by
developed countries
to  farmers
†364. SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred
Question 2374, given in the Rajya Sabha
on the 13th December, 2002 and state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the subsidy
being given by America and other developed
countries to their farmers on a large scale in
agriculture sector is against the agreement
with World Trade Organisation;
(b) if so, whether the subsidy by these
countries could not be banned through
World Trade Organisation; and
(c) if so, the future planning of India in
this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

80
Contract farming
†365. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to enact a law for contract
farming under pressure from various
companies;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government have not consulted farmers'
organisation in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Modernisation of handling,
storage and transportation
of foodgrains
366.SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH LIBRA:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken any
step to modernize the system of handling,
storage and transportation of foodgrains
within the country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Floriculture production
†367. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the total production
and the production per hectare in the
floriculture sector in the country
during the last three years, year-wise and
State-wise;
(b) the details of the demand and
producton of flowers in the country during
the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(c) whether Government propose to set
up a technology mission to increase the
flower-production; and
(d) the names and other details of the
Centrally sponsored schemes meant for
increasing the flower-production in the
country, specially in Bihar which faces
natural calamities like flood every year?
Details of workshop on
agriculture
368. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the observations made in a recent workshop
on "The Role of Biotechnology in
Agriculture" as to how biotech crops could
improve farming competitiveness and
reduce insecticide usage, its advantages in
oil-conservation and enhanced
productivity, improved water quality, etc.;
(b) if so, whether such suggestions are
being adopted to further improve our
agricultural productivity; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Production  of  fruits  and
vegetables in Uttaranchal
†369. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any specific scheme for
increasing the production of fruits including
apples grown in the moderate climate has
been formulated for Uttaranchal; and
(b) if so, the types of assistance
proposed to be provided by Government
to the State, in this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

81
